draft.title: Reproductive technologies
card: Reproductive technologies let people control which organisms breed together. They are used in farming and in medicine.
semen is collected from a chosen male and placed in a female's reproductive tract by people, not by mating. One male can father many offspring, even in distant places.
pollen is collected from a chosen plant and placed on the stigma of another chosen plant by people, not by wind or insects. It lets breeders choose both parent plants.
in vitro fertilisation joins egg and sperm in a laboratory dish. The embryo that forms is then placed in the uterus. It can help people who struggle to conceive naturally.
draft.remember: People choose the parents: sperm or pollen is moved by hand, and IVF fertilises the egg outside the body.

a.q: What do artificial insemination, artificial pollination and IVF have in common?
opts: People control which organisms breed together
They produce offspring identical to one parent
They add genes from a different species
They only work in animals, not in plants
a.why: In each method, people decide which gametes meet, so they choose the parents. None of them copies one parent or adds genes from another species. Offspring still come from fertilisation, so they are not identical to one parent.
a.clue: Think about who decides which parents are used.

b.q: Priya manages a dairy farm in Victoria. She wants calves from a bull on another continent that has never been to her farm. Which method would let her do this?
opts: Artificial insemination using semen from that bull
Artificial pollination using pollen from that bull
IVF, because the bull must be present in the dish
Letting her cows graze with other bulls nearby
b.why: Semen can be collected and transported, so artificial insemination lets a distant bull father calves. Artificial pollination is for plants, so it is wrong here. Grazing with other bulls leaves the choice of father to chance, not to Priya.
b.clue: Which method moves sperm without the male being present, and works in animals?

a.best: People control which organisms breed together

b.best: Artificial insemination using semen from that bull
